subject: History

internalBreakdown.component: Project: planning, organisation and data collection (August-October)
Project: viva by internal and external examiners

textbooks: Themes in Indian History, Part I (NCERT)
Themes in Indian History, Part II (NCERT)
Themes in Indian History, Part III (NCERT)
notes: Each theme introduces one type of source; the document lists only theme titles and learning outcomes, so topics are the theme's own subtitle and focus.
Question paper per part: 7 MCQ (1), 2 SA (3), 1 LA (8), 1 source-based (4) = 25.
Maps from the Survey of India website may be used.

units.name: Themes in Indian History Part I

chapters.name: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
topics: Early urban centres and social institutions
Aspects of the Harappan civilisation
Archaeological sources: viewpoints of the ASI and historians on Harappa
outcomes: Investigate and interpret early urban centres and social institutions
Deduce the multi-lateral aspects of the Harappan civilisation
Interpret historical and contemporary sources and viewpoints of the ASI and historians on Harappa

chapters.name: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies (c. 600 BCE-600 CE)
topics: Political and economic history of the subcontinent
Inscriptional evidence
outcomes: Evaluate major trends in the political and economic history of the subcontinent
Decode inscriptional evidence and how it shapes understanding of political and economic processes

chapters.name: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies (c. 600 BCE-600 CE)
topics: Social history
Social norms in the scriptures of ancient India
The Mahabharata as a source
outcomes: Analyse social norms to understand the perspectives of society in the scriptures of ancient India
Examine the dimensions historians have explored in the Mahabharata

chapters.name: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments (c. 600 BCE-600 CE)
topics: Major religious developments in early India
Religious sculpture, especially Buddhist sculpture
outcomes: Compare the major religious developments in early India
Interpret religious sculpture and the stories in it
Create a picture album of Buddhist sculpture

units.name: Themes in Indian History Part II

chapters.name: Through the Eyes of Travellers: Perceptions of Society (c. tenth to seventeenth centuries)
topics: Accounts of foreign travellers
Social, political and economic life under different rulers in the medieval period
outcomes: Understand the features of social histories described by travellers
Use foreign travellers' accounts to understand social, political and economic life in the medieval period

chapters.name: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: Changes in Religious Beliefs and Devotional Texts (c. eighth to eighteenth centuries)
topics: Religious developments
Philosophies of Bhakti and Sufi saints
Devotional texts
outcomes: Summarise the philosophies of Bhakti and Sufi saints
Comprehend how religious movements sought unity, peace and harmony

chapters.name: An Imperial Capital: Vijayanagara (c. fourteenth to sixteenth centuries)
topics: Architecture of the Vijayanagara empire
Foreign travellers' accounts of Vijayanagara
City planning, water management and administration
outcomes: Classify the architectural contributions of the Vijayanagara empire
Interpret political, social and cultural life of the city from travellers' accounts
Assess city planning, water management and administration

chapters.name: Peasants, Zamindars and the State: Agrarian Society and the Mughal Empire (c. sixteenth-seventeenth centuries)
topics: Agrarian developments
Relationship between the state and agriculture in the Mughal period
Agrarian change in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries
outcomes: Understand the relationship between the state and agriculture in the Mughal period
Compare agrarian changes of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries

units.name: Themes in Indian History Part III

chapters.name: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives
topics: Revenue systems introduced by the British
Colonial official records and reports
outcomes: Evaluate British revenue systems to understand the economics of colonisation
Analyse colonial records to understand divergent British and Indian interests

chapters.name: Rebels and the Raj: The Revolt of 1857 and its Representations
topics: Events of 1857
Planning and coordination of the rebels
Spread of the revolt and the vision of unity
Visual representations
outcomes: Examine the events of 1857 and the planning and coordination of the rebels
Analyse how the revolt created a vision of unity
Interpret nationalist and British visual images

chapters.name: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: Civil Disobedience and Beyond
topics: The nationalist movement in chronological order
Ideas, individuals and institutions under Gandhian leadership
Sources: newspapers, biographies, autobiographies, diaries, letters
outcomes: Correlate the elements of the nationalist movement under Gandhian leadership
Debate Gandhi's contributions and mass appeal
Interpret sources such as newspapers, autobiographies and letters

chapters.name: Framing the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era
topics: Role of the Constituent Assembly
Debates on important issues in the Constituent Assembly
outcomes: Highlight the role of the Constituent Assembly in framing the Constitution
Analyse how Constituent Assembly debates shaped the Constitution

chapters.name: Map Work (Indian History)
topics: Mature Harappan sites: Harappa, Banawali, Kalibangan, Balakot, Rakhigarhi, Dholavira, Nageshwar, Lothal, Mohenjodaro, Chanhudaro, Kot Diji
Mahajanapadas and cities: Vajji, Magadha, Kosala, Kuru, Panchala, Gandhara, Avanti, Rajgir, Ujjain, Taxila, Varanasi
Ashokan pillar inscriptions (Sanchi, Topra, Meerut, Kaushambi); kingdoms of the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas
Kushanas, Shakas, Satavahanas, Vakatakas, Guptas; Mathura, Kanauj, Puhar, Bharukachchha, Shravasti, Rajgir, Vaishali, Varanasi, Vidisha
Major Buddhist sites: Nagarjunakonda, Sanchi, Amaravati, Lumbini, Bharhut, Bodh Gaya, Ajanta
Bidar, Golconda, Bijapur, Vijayanagar, Chandragiri, Kanchipuram, Mysore, Thanjavur, Kolar, Tirunelveli
Territories under Babur, Akbar and Aurangzeb: Delhi, Agra, Panipat, Amber, Ajmer, Lahore, Goa
Territories under British control in 1857: Punjab, Sindh, Bombay, Madras, Berar, Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, Surat, Calcutta, Patna, Allahabad
Main centres of the Revolt of 1857: Delhi, Meerut, Jhansi, Lucknow, Kanpur, Azamgarh, Calcutta, Benaras, Gwalior, Jabalpur, Agra, Awadh
Centres of the National Movement: Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad, Benaras, Amritsar, Chauri Chaura, Lahore, Bardoli, Dandi, Bombay, Karachi
